questions.prompt: Rainfall at a site is estimated from two gauges by inverse distance weighting with weights 1/d². Gauge A, 2 km away, recorded 40 mm; gauge B, 4 km away, recorded 60 mm. What is the estimate at the site, in mm? Give it to one decimal.

Two pairs of boreholes about 1 km apart have soil lead concentrations of (120, 130) and (100, 120) mg/kg. Using only these two pairs, what is the semivariance γ at 1 km, in (mg/kg)²? Give it to one decimal.
questions.explanation: γ(h) = ½ × the average of the squared differences: the differences are 10 and 20, squared 100 and 400, average 250, half of it 125.0. A real variogram uses every pair at each distance.

questions.prompt: A variogram of groundwater levels rises from a nugget of 0.3 m² to a sill of 4.0 m², which it reaches at a range of 6 km. What does the range tell a hydrologist?
options: Wells more than about 6 km apart are no more alike than any two random wells, so a well that far away says nothing about the level at a site
The water level varies by 6 m across the aquifer
The interpolation error is 6 m everywhere
questions.explanation: The range is the distance at which the semivariance reaches the sill: beyond it, values are uncorrelated. Within it, nearby wells help predict a site, the more the closer they are.

questions.prompt: Two boreholes drilled 1 m apart give quite different contaminant concentrations. On a variogram, which feature does that show?
options: A large nugget: variation over very short distances, or measurement error
questions.explanation: The nugget is the semivariance as the distance goes to zero. If even neighbouring samples differ, the nugget is large: some of the variation is noise, or happens on a scale finer than the sampling.

questions.prompt: What does kriging give that inverse distance weighting does not?
options: Weights chosen from a fitted variogram, and an estimate of the error at every point of the map
questions.explanation: Kriging uses the variogram model to choose the weights that make the estimate unbiased with the least error, and it gives the kriging variance: the uncertainty of each estimate. Inverse distance weighting has neither a model nor an error.
